title: Local dimension at a group identity equals global dimension
statement: Let $k$ be any field and $G$ a group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type over $k$. Let $e\in G$ be the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ under its identity section. Then $\dim\mathcal O_{G,e}=\dim G$, with local Krull dimension and the topological Krull dimension of $G$ in $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$. No reducedness, smoothness or characteristic assumption is required.

source.place: Dimension paragraph; sk-i-cartier third proof paragraph

proof.text: Construct the pullback H of G to the actual algebraic closure K of k, with its functorially induced group-object structure. The base change q of the identity section is the universal pullback lift. The rational-point local-dimension comparison equates the original identity stalk dimension with the dimension at q in H.

Over K, the rational point q is closed by pointEquivClosedPoint. Every point specializes to a closed point by compactness of H. Translations act transitively on closed points, giving homeomorphisms and hence equality of their coheights. Mathlib ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight, coheight_anti and IsOpenEmbedding.coheight_eq show that every stalk dimension is bounded by the dimension at q. The supremum defining Scheme.dim is therefore this value, and Scheme.dim_eq_topologicalKrullDim identifies it with global dimension. This is proved directly in rational_dimension_algClosed.

Choose matching affine covers of G and H under field extension. Scheme.dim_eq_iSup_ringKrullDim_of_affineOpenCover expresses both dimensions as suprema of chart dimensions. The first clause of dim_base_change identifies the tensor-product ring dimension on every chart. This proves dimension_field_baseChange and descends the global dimension to G. Combine the three equalities.
